chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man plucks the hairs of his two armpits after entering the state of Ihram, he is liable for a blood sacrifice (dam).

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood sacrifice (a specific type of expiation offering)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for plucking armpit hair while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Ishtibār clarifies the specific expiation (dam) required for plucking armpit hair during Ihram, distinguishing it from shaving or general hair removal. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the precision of ritual purity laws, where the act of plucking (notaf) is treated as a distinct violation requiring a sacrificial animal, reflecting the broader principle that minor breaches of Ihram sanctity demand tangible atonement.
